compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`make verify` — the stated CI contract in `AGENTS.md` — cannot pass on a host
where any other rebar process is running a gate. `make test` runs pytest with
`-n 4` (four xdist workers), and the gate-admission cap
(`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:299` `gate_admission`) is **4 slots that are
HOST-GLOBAL**, not per-repo, per-worktree or per-test-session: `_slot_dir()`
(`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:210`) puts the slot files under the snapshot
store root's `locks/`, i.e. `$TMPDIR/rebar-gate-snapshots/locks/gate-slot-N`.

So the four test workers must win all four host slots at once. Any other rebar
gate process on the box takes one and the suite starts failing with
`GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots busy`.

## Evidence

Three `make verify` runs in one session on this host, same commit, all green in
lint + typecheck, all failing only on gate admission — with a DIFFERENT failure
set each time (15, then 9 on a subset re-run, then 26), which is the signature of
a contended shared resource rather than a code defect:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py::... - GateCongestedError: gate
      admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots busy

Confirmed holder during one run:

    60942 /Users/joeoakhart/scanner-promote/.venv/bin/rebar review-plan
          guileless-emeritus-izuthrush

— a DIFFERENT worktree's plan review, holding `gate-slot-0` for its whole run.
Each affected test passes when its file is run alone, and the same multi-file
selection passes on unmodified `main`, so the failures track host load, not the
tree. The same commit that failed locally took `Verified +1` from CI
(GitHub Actions, an isolated runner with no competing rebar processes).

## Why this matters

`AGENTS.md` makes `make verify` the ONLY local command that lets an agent say "I
verified this" and be right, and warns that three changes were pushed red in one
week by people who ran `make lint` instead. On a shared developer box that runs
the MCP server and parallel agents — which is exactly how this project is worked
— `make verify` is instead a coin flip, and its failures look like real test
failures. That trains agents to dismiss red `make verify` output, which defeats
the whole point of the contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The scope mismatch is confirmed: `make test`'s worker count and the
      gate-admission slot count are shown to contend, with the slot store's
      host-global location cited.
- [ ] AC2 A test-session gate run cannot be starved by an unrelated rebar
      process on the same host — e.g. the admission slot store is scoped per
      test session (or per repo/worktree) rather than per host, or the test
      suite's gate path does not consume the operator-facing cap at all.
- [ ] AC3 The operator-facing purpose of the cap — bounding concurrent gate
      memory on one machine — is preserved for real gate runs; the fix must not
      simply raise or disable the cap.
- [ ] AC4 A test demonstrates the starvation before the fix and its absence
      after, without depending on wall-clock timing.
- [ ] AC5 `make verify` completes with no `GateCongestedError` on a host that is
      concurrently running an unrelated `rebar review-plan`.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. Do not raise the cap as the fix (AC3).
compiled_state.title: make verify cannot pass on a host running any other rebar gate: 4 xdist workers contend for 4 HOST-GLOBAL admission slots
